title: Acute Poisoning and Overdose
sourceTitle: Resuscitation Council UK 2025 Special Circumstances Guidelines
scope: Adults in cardiac arrest or peri-arrest where poisoning is suspected; this extraction is limited to resuscitation priorities and poison-centre escalation.
gaps: The source does not provide a complete toxin-specific investigation set, antidote doses, routes, frequencies, durations or contraindications. Obtain poison-centre advice and reconcile with Saudi toxicology and formulary protocols before approval.

investigations.test: ABCDE assessment with continuous physiological monitoring
investigations.question: Is there immediately reversible airway, breathing, circulation or neurological compromise?
investigations.finding: Clinical instability or a toxidrome may identify urgent supportive priorities.
investigations.rationale: The guideline directs structured assessment and correction of reversible causes in toxic cardiac arrest.

investigations.question: Which toxic agent, dose, timing and specific treatment are relevant?
investigations.finding: Agent-specific advice may identify antidotes, decontamination or enhanced elimination.
investigations.rationale: The guideline directs consultation with a regional or national poison centre.
investigations.timeframe: As soon as poisoning is suspected

actions.instruction: Ensure responder safety and avoid direct exposure to potentially transmissible toxic agents.
Reduce further absorption and consider antidotes, decontamination and enhanced elimination only with agent-specific expert advice.
Prepare for prolonged resuscitation because toxin concentration may fall during metabolism or elimination.

title: Acute Severe Asthma Exacerbation
sourceTitle: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN)
scope: Adults and young people who are acutely unwell or highly symptomatic at presentation; limited to immediate treatment, objective testing and post-attack action-plan review.
gaps: NG245 signposts retained BTS/SIGN acute-attack guidance and does not give a complete acute severe asthma drug/dose table on this page. Exact bronchodilator, oxygen and corticosteroid doses, contraindications and escalation thresholds require current acute-attack and Saudi/local protocol reconciliation.

investigations.test: Objective testing available during acute presentation
investigations.question: Can asthma be objectively supported without delaying treatment?
investigations.finding: Eosinophil count, FeNO, spirometry or peak expiratory flow before and after bronchodilator may support diagnosis.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends immediate treatment while performing available objective tests in acutely unwell or highly symptomatic people.

investigations.question: Were objective tests unreliable or unavailable during the attack?
investigations.finding: Testing after control may confirm asthma and reduce treatment-related false-normal results.
investigations.rationale: NICE advises completing objective testing after acute symptoms are controlled when it cannot be done immediately.

actions.instruction: Treat immediately when the person is acutely unwell or highly symptomatic; do not delay treatment for diagnostic testing.
Review the personalised asthma action plan after an acute consultation, emergency attendance or hospital admission.
actions.timeframe: Before discharge or at the acute review

title: Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding
sourceTitle: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
scope: People aged over 16 with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding; limited to risk assessment, resuscitation-linked endoscopy timing and selected named treatments.
gaps: The recommendation page names prothrombin complex concentrate, proton pump inhibitors and terlipressin but does not provide complete dose, route, frequency, duration or contraindication data. Local massive-haemorrhage, anticoagulant-reversal, variceal-bleed and formulary protocols are required before approval.

investigations.question: What is the pre-endoscopy risk and is early discharge potentially appropriate?
investigations.finding: A score of 0 identifies people for whom early discharge may be considered.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends the Blatchford score at first assessment.

investigations.question: What is the bleeding source and is endoscopic haemostasis required?
investigations.finding: Endoscopy identifies variceal or non-variceal bleeding and stigmata of recent haemorrhage.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends immediate endoscopy after resuscitation for unstable severe bleeding and within 24 hours for other patients.
investigations.timeframe: Immediately after resuscitation if unstable; otherwise within 24 hours of admission

actions.instruction: Offer endoscopy to unstable patients with severe bleeding immediately after resuscitation; offer it within 24 hours to all other patients.
For non-variceal bleeding, do not use adrenaline alone; use a recommended mechanical, thermal, fibrin or thrombin method with or without adrenaline as specified by NICE.
Offer terlipressin at presentation when variceal bleeding is suspected, then stop after definitive haemostasis or after 5 days unless another indication exists.
actions.timeframe: At presentation through definitive haemostasis, maximum 5 days per the recommendation

title: Adult Essential Hypertension Screening and Confirmation
sourceTitle: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management
scope: Adults undergoing blood-pressure measurement, confirmation of hypertension and target-organ-damage assessment.
gaps: This extraction does not select a specific antihypertensive product or dose. Pregnancy, chronic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, frailty, resistant hypertension and Saudi/local thresholds require dedicated reconciliation before approval.

investigations.test: Standardised clinic blood pressure in both arms
investigations.question: Is clinic blood pressure raised and is there a persistent inter-arm difference?
investigations.finding: Clinic blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or higher prompts repeat measurement and confirmation; a persistent inter-arm difference over 15 mmHg directs future measurements to the higher arm.
investigations.rationale: NICE specifies standardised technique, repeat measurement and bilateral assessment.

investigations.test: Ambulatory or home blood pressure monitoring
investigations.question: Is hypertension confirmed outside the clinic?
investigations.finding: A daytime ABPM or HBPM average of 135/85 mmHg or higher with clinic pressure at least 140/90 mmHg confirms hypertension.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends ABPM, or HBPM when ABPM is unsuitable, for confirmation below severe-hypertension thresholds.
investigations.timeframe: After raised clinic blood pressure is identified

investigations.question: Is there renal, metabolic, retinal or cardiac involvement?
investigations.finding: Urine ACR and haematuria testing, HbA1c, electrolytes, creatinine/eGFR, cholesterol, fundoscopy and 12-lead ECG identify associated risk or damage.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends this assessment for all people with hypertension.

actions.instruction: Offer lifestyle advice to people with suspected or diagnosed hypertension and repeat it periodically.
actions.timeframe: From initial assessment and at review

actions.instruction: Provide annual review for adults with hypertension to monitor blood pressure and discuss lifestyle, symptoms and medication.

title: Adult Periodic Health Examination
sourceTitle: US Preventive Services Task Force A and B Recommendations
locator: A and B Recommendations table; eligibility and recommendation-date columns
scope: Asymptomatic adults considered for preventive services; each service remains conditional on the population, age, sex, pregnancy and risk criteria stated in its linked recommendation.
gaps: This index is not a Saudi periodic-health-examination schedule and does not replace service-specific recommendation statements. Every proposed screen needs current Saudi eligibility, interval, test method, harms and referral-pathway reconciliation; no medicine regimen is supported by this extraction.

investigations.test: Age-, sex-, pregnancy- and risk-based preventive eligibility review
investigations.question: Which current USPSTF grade A or B services apply to this individual?
investigations.finding: Only services whose linked population criteria match the individual should be offered or discussed.
investigations.rationale: The source is an index of preventive services with moderate or substantial net benefit for defined populations.

actions.instruction: Open the current service-specific recommendation before ordering a screen and document that its population and risk criteria apply.
Reconcile selected services with current Saudi Ministry of Health programmes and local referral capacity.

title: Adult Vaccination Review
sourceTitle: CDC Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule for Ages 19 Years or Older
edition: United States, 2025 schedule currently displayed by CDC under court-order notice
locator: Tables 1 and 2, Notes, and Appendix on contraindications and precautions
scope: Adults aged 19 years or older reviewed by age, vaccination history, medical condition and other indication using the current CDC-hosted schedule.
gaps: This is a United States schedule and must be reconciled with the current Saudi national immunisation schedule, locally available products and product information. Product-specific dose volume, route, contraindications and special-population rules must be rechecked before prescribing or administration.

investigations.test: Documented vaccine history and age review
investigations.question: Which routine vaccine series are complete, due or missing?
investigations.finding: The age table and notes identify candidate routine and catch-up vaccines.
investigations.rationale: CDC directs clinicians to determine recommendations by age and then consult the notes.

investigations.question: Do comorbidities create an indication, contraindication or precaution?
investigations.finding: The medical-condition table and appendix identify additional indications and safety restrictions.
investigations.rationale: CDC requires condition-based review and the contraindications/precautions appendix before administration.

actions.instruction: Determine recommended vaccines by age, then assess medical-condition indications, dosing intervals, special situations, contraindications and precautions in the linked notes and appendix.
Defer a vaccine when a listed precaution is present unless an individual benefit-risk assessment supports administration; do not administer when a listed contraindication is present.

title: Advanced COPD Supportive Care
sourceTitle: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in over 16s: diagnosis and management
edition: NG115, palliative-care recommendations retained from 2004 and linked standards updated 2018
scope: People with end-stage COPD whose breathlessness is unresponsive to other medical therapy and their families or carers.
gaps: NICE names opioids, benzodiazepines, tricyclic antidepressants, major tranquillisers and oxygen but gives no exact dose, route, frequency, duration or complete contraindication set in these recommendations. Specialist palliative, respiratory and Saudi formulary review is mandatory before any medicine order.

investigations.question: Is breathlessness persistent despite optimised disease-directed treatment and what services are needed?
investigations.finding: Refractory breathlessness and patient/family needs may support palliative-team involvement.
investigations.rationale: The NICE section applies medicine considerations only when end-stage COPD breathlessness remains unresponsive and recommends access to multidisciplinary palliative services.
investigations.timeframe: When symptoms remain refractory or needs change

actions.instruction: Provide access to the full range of multidisciplinary palliative-care services, including hospice admission when appropriate.
Consider an opioid for refractory breathlessness only after other medical therapy has not relieved it and with specialist/local prescribing review.
Consider benzodiazepines, tricyclic antidepressants, major tranquillisers or oxygen only when appropriate for refractory breathlessness and after individual benefit-risk review.

title: Advanced Dementia and Comfort-Focused Care
sourceTitle: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
edition: NG97, published 20 June 2018; surveillance review 24 October 2025
scope: People living with advanced or severe dementia, including those approaching the end of life, and their families or carers.
gaps: The source provides care principles rather than exact symptom-control prescriptions. Medicine names, doses, routes, frequencies, durations and contraindications require an individualised palliative plan, current care-of-dying guidance and Saudi/local formulary review.

investigations.question: What comfort, communication, nutrition, safety and end-of-life needs are present and can the person participate in decisions?
investigations.finding: The assessment informs flexible palliative care, advance planning and best-interest decisions where capacity is absent.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends needs-based palliative care from diagnosis and anticipatory healthcare planning near end of life.
investigations.timeframe: From diagnosis and whenever needs or prognosis change

investigations.question: Can the person eat and drink safely and is specialist swallowing input required?
investigations.finding: Swallowing concern may prompt speech and language therapy involvement.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends supporting eating and drinking and considering speech and language therapy for safety concerns.
investigations.timeframe: When eating or drinking concerns arise

actions.instruction: Offer flexible, needs-based palliative care and use anticipatory healthcare planning when the person is approaching end of life.
actions.timeframe: From diagnosis and as end of life approaches

actions.instruction: Balance current medical needs against the harms of hospital admission and consider advance plans and the value of familiar surroundings.
Do not routinely use enteral feeding in severe dementia unless a potentially reversible comorbidity indicates it.

title: Advanced Heart Failure Supportive Care
sourceTitle: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management
scope: Adults with heart failure whose symptoms are worsening despite optimal specialist treatment, including advance planning and end-of-life support.
gaps: The palliative-care recommendations do not provide exact symptom-control medicine doses, routes, frequencies, durations or contraindications. Current heart-failure therapy, renal function, device management, care-of-dying guidance and Saudi/local formulary requirements need specialist reconciliation before approval.

investigations.question: Are symptoms worsening despite optimal specialist treatment and are palliative services required?
investigations.finding: Unresolved symptom burden may trigger MDT discussion and palliative-needs assessment.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends discussion with the specialist heart-failure MDT when symptoms worsen despite optimal treatment.
investigations.timeframe: When symptoms worsen or care goals change

investigations.question: Does continued activation remain consistent with current goals of care?
investigations.finding: A documented review may support continuation or advance planning for deactivation.
investigations.rationale: NICE recommends review every 6 months, whenever goals change and during end-of-life advance planning.
investigations.timeframe: Every 6 months, on goal changes, and during advance care planning

actions.instruction: Discuss palliative needs with the specialist heart-failure MDT and consider a formal palliative-needs assessment when symptoms worsen despite optimal treatment.
actions.timeframe: At recognition of worsening refractory symptoms

actions.instruction: Offer the person and family or carers access to professionals with palliative-care skills within the heart-failure team.
Do not offer long-term home oxygen solely for advanced heart failure; assess separate comorbid indications if present.
